channel.title: Elevate · The Entertrainer Blogs
channel.description: Articles about work, learning, technology, and the questions that stay with you.

item.title: Hot Tea, Dead Phones, and Why Rest Is Not a Moral Failure
item.description: A small physics story about rest, hot tea, batteries, deleted files, and why the universe likes to spread things out. Read time: ? minutes.

item.title: Friend, friendly. Love, lovely. So why isn’t the Moon moonly?
item.description: English will build an adjective out of almost any noun, then quietly refuse for the Moon, the Sun and your own teeth. The reason is older than English. Read time: ? minutes.

item.title: Why Staring at a Word Long Enough Can Make It Stop Being a Word
item.description: One evening at work I stared at the word "door" until it stopped looking like English. That glitch has a name, an Ig Nobel Prize, and a family of stranger cousins. Read time: ? minutes.

item.title: The Midpoint of Your Life Isn't 40. It's 18.
item.description: A video I watched claimed the real midpoint of an 81-year life is age 18, not 40. The maths behind it is genuine, two centuries old — and shakier than the confident voiceover made it sound. Read time: ? minutes.

item.title: You Only Find Out You Don’t Know It When You Have to Explain It
item.description: The feeling of knowing arrives first, and cheaply. A zip, a policy, a search bar — they all sell you a working model. The model is often just a label with good lighting. Read time: ? minutes.

item.title: Tajjalan
item.description: An old word from the Chāndogya Upaniṣad: whatever shows up is born from That, lives in That, and returns into That. Read time: ? minutes.

item.title: How many of you, is actually inside you?
item.description: Surgeons cut the cable between the brain halves for epilepsy. Speech said it saw nothing. The left hand still found the key. Then the mouth built a chicken-shed story for a shovel it never chose. Read time: ? minutes.

item.title: 396 to 528 is a fourth, not a lost scale
item.description: Play 396 hertz, then 528. That jump is a perfect fourth. The nine-tone list around it is still sold as a scale a medieval monk forgot. Read time: 9 minutes.
